title: Chatter on SS304 finishing pass
action: Drop feed to 0.12 mm/rev, raise speed about 10% and keep tool stick-out under 30 mm.
why: Above 0.2 mm/rev on SS304 the 2-flute cutter vibrates and the spindle bearings take the hit. Every bearing failure on VMC-3 started with chatter.
author: Ramesh

title: चैटर आए तो क्या करें
action: स्टिक-आउट कम करो, फीड 0.12 रखो, RPM थोड़ा बढ़ाओ। आवाज़ न जाए तो मशीन रोको।
why: चैटर से स्पिंडल बेअरिंग खराब होता है, VMC-3 पर पहले कई बार हुआ है।
author: Ramesh

title: Spindle whine before bearing failure
action: If the spindle whines at idle around 8000 rpm, check spindle temperature. Above 55 °C stop and call maintenance.
why: The last bearing failures started with this sound 1–2 weeks before.
author: Ramesh

title: Spindle warm-up in winter
action: Run warm-up program O9001 for 10 minutes, 2000 to 6000 rpm, before the first job.
why: Cold grease makes the bearings run hot and the first parts go oversize.
author: Ramesh

title: Vibration with the 50 mm face mill
action: Check every insert is seated; replace all 4 inserts together, never one.
why: One new insert sticks out and makes the cutter unbalanced.
author: Ramesh

title: Pull-stud check on tool holders
action: Check pull-stud torque every Monday on all holders in the magazine.
why: A loose stud gives runout and breaks the 10 mm end mill.
author: Ramesh

title: Flange thickness drifting
action: Blow the vise jaws and seat clean before every part.
why: One chip under the jaw tilts the part by 0.05 mm.
author: Ramesh

title: Coolant aim on deep pockets
action: Point the second nozzle straight into the pocket, not at the tool shank.
why: Chips re-cut in a dry pocket and ruin the finish.
author: Ramesh

title: Coolant pump gland leak
action: Tighten gland nut a quarter turn; if it still drips, change the seal kit.
why: A leaking gland lets air in and the pump loses pressure.
author: Ramesh

title: Y-axis backlash after long idle
action: After a weekend, run the axis warm-up and measure a test bore before production.
why: Ways are dry after idle and the first parts are off by 0.02 mm.
author: Ramesh

title: Alarm 1012 spindle orientation
action: Re-home the spindle with M19; if it repeats, check the proximity sensor gap is 0.8 mm.
why: The sensor bracket loosens with vibration.
author: Ramesh

title: Conveyor jam with stringy SS chips
action: Use inserts with a chip breaker on SS304 and clear the conveyor at shift end.
why: Long stringy chips wrap the conveyor and stall the motor.
author: Ramesh

title: Burr on FL-101 holes
action: After drilling, run the 90° chamfer tool at feed 0.05 mm/rev.
why: QC rejects for burr stopped after we added this step.
author: Ramesh

title: HSS drill breaking in SS304
action: Peck drill with 1 mm pecks at 600 rpm and full flood coolant.
why: SS304 work-hardens; a dwelling drill rubs and snaps.
author: Ramesh

title: Mirror finish on SS304 flange face
action: Leave 0.2 mm for finish, climb mill, use a fresh insert edge.
why: A worn edge rubs instead of cutting and smears the surface.
author: Ramesh

title: Reading chip colour on SS304
action: Silver or straw chips are fine. Blue chips with a carbide tool mean too hot: reduce speed 10% or check coolant. Blue chips with HSS: stop and reduce speed.
why: Chip colour shows cutting temperature before the tool or spindle suffers.
author: Ramesh

title: Built-up edge on Al6061
action: Keep coolant concentration at 8% and use polished 3-flute end mills.
why: Aluminium welds to a dry or rough edge.
author: Suresh

title: ATC arm alarm after power cut
action: Re-teach the tool change position from the maintenance screen before restarting.
why: The arm loses its reference when power drops mid-change.
author: Suresh

title: Ramp into pockets, never plunge
action: Ramp at 3° into Al6061 pockets with the 10 mm end mill.
why: Plunging a centre-cutting end mill packs chips and breaks it.
author: Suresh

title: Check coolant with the refractometer
action: Measure concentration every Monday; top up to 8%.
why: Low concentration caused the BR-310 finish rejects.
author: Suresh

title: Tool length offset after insert change
action: Re-measure tool length on the setter every time an insert or holder changes.
why: An old offset made BR-310 pockets 0.1 mm deep.
author: Suresh

title: Aluminium chips should stay bright
action: Dull grey or smeared chips mean built-up edge: clean the tool, check coolant.
why: Aluminium does not change colour with heat like steel does.
author: Suresh

title: Taper from worn chuck jaws
action: Re-bore soft jaws when OD taper is above 0.02 mm over 100 mm.
why: Worn jaws hold the shaft at a tilt.
author: Suresh

title: Long shaft chatter
action: Use the tailstock for any overhang longer than 3 times the diameter.
why: An unsupported shaft bends and vibrates.
author: Suresh

title: Insert nose radius for EN8 finish
action: Use 0.8 mm nose radius at feed 0.15 for finish passes.
why: Bigger radius and lower feed give Ra 1.6 without grinding.
author: Suresh

title: Chuck pressure for thin parts
action: Lower chuck pressure to 12 bar for thin-wall parts.
why: Full pressure squeezes the part oval.
author: Suresh

title: Boring bar overhang
action: Keep boring bar overhang under 4 times its diameter; use the carbide bar beyond that.
why: A long steel bar sings and leaves chatter marks.
author: Suresh

title: Coolant on EN8 roughing
action: Flood coolant on roughing; direct the nozzle at the insert tip.
why: Hot chips weld to the insert and break it.
author: Suresh

title: चक जॉ साफ ठेवा
action: प्रत्येक पार्टनंतर जॉ हवेने साफ करा, मग पुढचा पार्ट लावा।
why: जॉमध्ये चिप अडकली तर शाफ्ट तिरका बसतो।
author: Suresh

title: Carriage gib noise
action: If the carriage knocks on direction change, adjust the gib screws.
why: A loose gib lets the carriage rock and spoils the finish.
author: Suresh

title: Cleaned coolant nozzle
action: Nozzle was blocked, cleaned it and finish improved.
author: Priya

title: Check part seating
action: Part was not seated, tapped it down with a soft hammer.
author: Priya
